ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a vertical multiplication. The three-digit number on top is written as “***”, and the three-digit multiplier below is written as “1**”. Under the horizontal line, three partial products are listed, displayed in order as “22**”, “90*”, and “**2”, with a plus sign beside them; the final total product at the bottom is displayed as “56***”. Reasoning: Let the upper three-digit number be N, and the lower multiplier be 100+10d+e. The third partial product “**2” comes from multiplying N by the 1 in the hundreds place of the multiplier, so N itself is a three-digit number whose units digit is 2, denoted N=100a+10b+2. The second partial product is “90*”, so N·d is a three-digit number between 900 and 909. Combining this with the fact that the units digit of N is 2, screen the one-digit number d one by one: possible results are (d,N)=(1,902),(2,452),(3,302). Then use the first partial product “22**” to screen, that is, it is required that 2200≤N·e≤2299. If N=902, there is no one-digit number e that makes the product fall between 2200 and 2299; if N=302, there is also no one-digit number e satisfying it; if N=452, then when e=5, 452×5=2260, matching “22**”. Therefore N=452, and the multiplier is 125. The complete multiplication is 452×125=56500, which also matches the final “56***”. The sum of the digits of the product is 5+6+5+0+0=16.

method.method_draft: Read the vertical multiplication from the image as a 3-digit number N = *** multiplied by a 3-digit number 1**, with partial products shown as 22**, 90*, and **2, and final product 56***. From the third partial product **2, which is the multiplicand times the hundreds digit 1, infer that the multiplicand itself ends in 2, so write N = 100a + 10b + 2. Let the multiplier be 100 + 10d + e. Use the second partial product: N·d is a 3-digit number of the form 90*, so 900 ≤ N·d ≤ 909. Test possible one-digit d values with N ending in 2; this forces d = 2 and N = 452, because 452·2 = 904. Then use the first partial product: N·e has the form 22**, so 2200 ≤ 452e ≤ 2299, giving e = 5 since 452·5 = 2260. Thus the full product is 452·125 = 56500, whose digit sum is 5 + 6 + 5 + 0 + 0 = 16.
